subject: Pilot top-up request and risk mitigation plan – Crescendo Analytics bake-off
messages:
From: Pete Larsson <pete@crescendo.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Linda Chen <linda.chen@crescendo.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: additional evaluation credits and variant access for Crescendo bake-off

Hi Ava,

Quick one — Crescendo is running a short RFP bake-off against HydraAI (vendor) and the technical team needs to run a blind head-to-head over the next 10 business days. Our procurement deadline is Nov 12, so we need a fast turnaround.

Specifically we’re asking for:
- A top-up of 300k tokens to our trial account to complete the stress/latency/quality runs
- Access to a quantized variant (if available) so the comparison is fair on cost/latency

We reviewed your public perf sheets but need sandbox parity during the bake-off. We can sign a short pilot SLA or mutual NDA if that helps. Also, please include any SOC2/retention notes we’ll need for procurement.

Can we get confirmation by EOD Nov 2? If 300k is a blocker, what’s the largest immediate top-up you can provide and any caveats?

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

Pete
Pete Larsson
Head of ML Engineering, Crescendo Analytics
procurement@crescendo.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: crescedemo_spec.docx (stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Pete Larsson <pete@crescendo.ai>
Cc: Linda Chen <linda.chen@crescendo.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: additional evaluation credits and variant access for Crescendo bake-off

Hi Pete — thanks for the note and context. Helpful to know the deadline.

Short answer: we can support the bake-off but want to balance risk and precedent for credits. Proposed package we can get started on immediately:

- Provision 200,000 tokens to your trial account today (one-time top-up)
- Temporary access to our q8 quantized serving variant for the duration of the pilot (subject to model/version compatibility)
- A 2-day sandbox extension tied to the top-up window (rolls back after the run)

Ask from our side: Crescendo signs a short pilot SLA that limits reuse of the credit for public benchmarks and confirms data handling (I’ve attached a one‑page pilot SLA). That keeps the commercial offer contained and lets our ops team provision quickly.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Pete/Linda confirm acceptance of the q8 trial + 200k tokens and sign the attached pilot SLA (crescendo-pilot-sla.pdf).
2) Rafael — can you validate if there are any model/arch constraints for Crescendo’s test harness and add a short config they can drop into their harness?
3) Monica — can you own provisioning and cost-monitoring alerts? I’ll copy ops to start the top-up once we have SLA confirmation.

If 200k is not sufficient to run a head-to-head for the full test matrix, tell us which test buckets matter most (latency P95, throughput, eng-probing adversarial inputs) and we’ll re-evaluate a one-off increase.

I’ll hold the final approval from leadership while we get legal to sign.

Ava Chen
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0128

Attachments: crescendo-pilot-sla.pdf (one-page pilot), sample-inference-config.yaml (stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Pete Larsson <pete@crescendo.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: additional evaluation credits and variant access for Crescendo bake-off

Pete — quick technical note from my side to make the head-to-head meaningful and reproducible: 

- Use the q8 quantized variant (we’ll enable it on your trial account). q8 gives a good cost/latency tradeoff; for parity with HydraAI, pick our q8-rv1 checkpoint (I will pin the version on provisioning).
- Warm KV cache: run 3 short prefix warm-ups before your main runs to avoid cold start bias in latency numbers.
- Metrics to collect (minimum): latency P50/P95, tokens/sec, mem footprint, and error rate per prompt category.
- If you’re doing structured output tests, enable deterministic decoding seeds so results are repeatable.

I’m attaching a tiny config you can drop into your harness (sample-inference-config.yaml) that sets batching/streaming knobs and a small script to compute per-case cost. If we provision today I’ll help validate the first run tomorrow morning.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0166

Attachment: sample-inference-config.yaml (stub)

Thanks Ava & Rafael — Crescendo accepts the proposed package. Two confirmations from procurement side:

1) We will sign the one‑page pilot SLA (please send a DocuSign link) and acknowledge the non-public benchmark clause.
2) 200k tokens + q8 access is acceptable for the first phase; if we need additional tokens we’ll circle back with a narrowly scoped request and the specific test buckets.

Would you also attach a short invoice stub or PO-friendly line item for accounting? Our procurement needs that to create the internal PO.

If you can provision by Nov 4 morning PST, we’ll run the first warm-up and share initial numbers by Nov 6. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Linda Chen
